clue.text: Well enunciated, 'doe' and 'a name I call myself'?

indicators.note: to enunciate is to say clearly, so the words are to be taken by their sound

blocks.note: in the song a doe is 'a deer, a female deer'; deer is said the same as the spelling used here
the Sound of Music line for the note 'mi', which is the word for oneself

explanation.surface: Someone singing 'Do-Re-Mi' from The Sound of Music with careful diction.
explanation.walkthrough: Both quoted phrases come from the 'Do-Re-Mi' song: 'Doe, a deer' and 'Me, a name I call myself'. Say DEER and you have DEAR; then add ME.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation of mild surprise or dismay, 'Well!' and 'Dear me!' are interchangeable interjections.

clue.text: Duke covered by strange powders and moisture

definitions.note: the answer is plural; the definition is a mass noun

indicators.note: something covered by another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat smothered under odd powders and damp, like a cosmetics mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powders' sits in the surface as a cosmetic, but it is just letters to reshuffle; the duke's letter lands in the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beads of water that form on grass overnight are a visible kind of dampness, so the drops stand for the wetness itself.

clue.text: Worries when American soldiers surrounding gallery

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so one piece wraps around the others

blocks.note: 'as' can mean 'when', as in 'as I left'
GI is the usual term for a US soldier
the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: Anxiety arises when US troops close in on an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the famous London art gallery, a crossword favourite; 'when' is not a link word here but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or trouble them, a verb synonym for making them anxious.

clue.text: Offering grouse and beef, perhaps?

blocks.note: surface reading: serving game bird and meat as a dinner
setter's reading: to grouse and to beef both mean to complain, so this is an overdone fuss

explanation.surface: A host serving a dinner of game bird and roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouse and beef look like foods, which fits a literal meal, but both are also verbs meaning to complain at length, which is exactly what the idiom describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exaggerating a task or grievance, and complaining endlessly is overdoing something in just that way.

clue.text: Secretly thinks about coastal facilities

blocks.note: first meaning: keeps a thought or feeling hidden in mind, as with a grudge
second meaning: sheltered places where ships moor

explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads like a description of a plotter; it is the verb sense, as in nursing a grudge, while the second is the noun for ports.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means privately holding onto a suspicion; as a noun it names sheltered places where boats dock.

clue.text: When Frenchman's concealed top playing card is the absolute limit!

indicators.note: something concealed is tucked away inside, so one piece hides within another

blocks.note: the ace is the highest card in many games
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman cheating at cards by hiding an ace is beyond the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: M, short for Monsieur, sits inside ACE. The exclamation mark makes 'the absolute limit' sound like outrage, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the highest point or peak of something, so it is the utmost extent possible.

clue.text: Somewhat sombre, a king (Theban) kept demanding too much money

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following words is used
what is kept is held within, so the letters lie inside the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word through to the end of the bracketed one

explanation.surface: A gloomy king of Thebes who keeps asking for excessive sums.
explanation.walkthrough: It is sombRE A KING THEBAN; the K of 'kept' completes it, so 'kept' also provides its first letter after 'Theban'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something costing more than one can afford, which is the same as costing excessive sums.

clue.text: Some footballers, some soldiers and a journalist

blocks.note: a unit is a group of soldiers, so 'some soldiers' together
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A list of people: footballers, soldiers and a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'some' makes the three items look parallel, but the first is the definition: many British clubs are called United, such as Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Many football clubs, Manchester and Newcastle among them, carry this name, so a team of players can be referred to by it.

clue.text: Sibilant, harsh expostulation expressing seething huffiness, primarily?

definitions.text: Sibilant, harsh expostulation expressing seething huffiness, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the leading letters of the words are taken

blocks.clueFragment: Sibilant, harsh expostulation expressing seething huffiness
blocks.note: the opening letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style description of an exasperated hissing exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the description and the source letters; its hissing 's' and 'sh' sounds match the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection voices irritation or disbelief, and its hissing sounds make it exactly an annoyed sibilant outburst.

clue.text: Like something to beat eggs for sauce?

blocks.note: the kitchen tool for beating eggs
the suffix -y turns a noun into 'like that thing', as in 'silky'

explanation.surface: A cooking question: is this tool the thing for whipping eggs into a sauce?
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen setting makes 'sauce' look culinary, but it is slang for alcohol. Adding the adjective suffix Y to the tool makes 'like a whisk'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The sauce' is informal slang for alcoholic drink, and this Scotch spirit is one such drink.

clue.text: Idiot Everyman's anger about fence regularly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals skips every other letter, keeping the rest
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, says 'I am', shortened to I'M
bile is bad temper or anger
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: The setter fumes about a fence that keeps being overlooked, and is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for 'I am', so Everyman's gives IM. Then BILE goes around EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insulting terms for a stupid person, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Cars in landed properties

blocks.note: first meaning: estate cars, the British name for station wagons
second meaning: large country holdings of land

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an estate car is what Americans call a station wagon, so the plural can mean cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both station-wagon style vehicles and large tracts of land owned by one family.

clue.text: Organised resales around November for authenticity

indicators.note: to organise is to put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
around means encircling, so one piece goes about another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dealer arranges second-hand sales in November to prove items are genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange RESALES into REAL...ESS and put N in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe the quality of being genuine rather than fake, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Characters seen in riskier sports?

indicators.note: what is seen in something is visible inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asking which people take part in more dangerous sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' reads as people, but it also means letters: riSKIER Sports. The whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: People who race down snowy slopes on skis are participants in a dangerous sport, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Invariant, having peeled off, writhing in blissful state

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outermost letters are taken away
writhing is twisting about, so the letters twist into a new order

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something unchanging sheds its skin and squirms in a state of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer I and T, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the final state of release from suffering, and generally it means perfect happiness or peace.

clue.text: Arrangements being quiet acts of atonement

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
reparations are amends made for a wrong

explanation.surface: Plans made for quietly making amends.
explanation.walkthrough: P for piano is the musical marking meaning quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrangements made in advance of an event are the plans and readiness steps taken beforehand.

clue.text: Means of announcing arrival in refurbished bordello

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done up and rebuilt, so the letters are reconstructed

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A renovated brothel has a new way for visitors to signal they are there.
explanation.walkthrough: A bordello is a brothel; the device fits the scene neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors press a button by the entrance that rings inside, letting occupants know someone has come.

clue.text: Say a law's corrupt, typically

indicators.note: something corrupt is debased and spoilt, so the letters are put out of their proper order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that a law is, of course, dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', which suits 'typically', but it is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the usual or characteristic manner, so it can replace an adverb of habit.

clue.text: Scepticism is what hotel guests may need

blocks.note: first meaning: doubts or qualms about something
second meaning: bookings of rooms in advance

explanation.walkthrough: One word means both doubts and advance bookings.
explanation.definitionFit: Having doubts or misgivings about a plan, and booking a room ahead, are both expressed by this plural noun.

clue.text: Finally vanquish a queen and aged king

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter
taken as written
R is regina, Latin for queen
aged means old

explanation.surface: A queen finally defeats an elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for regina, as in royal signatures. The surface fits Harold, the English king finally vanquished at Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold II was the last Anglo-Saxon English monarch, killed in battle in 1066, so the name belongs to a ruler.

clue.text: Feels sorry for having run off at first seeing birds

indicators.note: having a thing go off at the front means the opening part is removed

blocks.note: to regret is to feel sorry
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone feels remorse for running off upon seeing birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Take REGRETS and drop the R from its front. R for run comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are white herons, long-legged wading birds, so the word names a type of bird.

clue.text: A diary not available for reflection somewhere in SW Africa

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
a log is a daily record
NA is the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A diary that cannot be consulted for thought, kept somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' sounds like thinking over a diary, but it means mirroring: the whole string of pieces is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This republic lies on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa, north of Namibia, so it is a place in that region.

clue.text: A whole number? That's essential

blocks.note: first meaning: in maths, relating to or being an integer
second meaning: necessary to make a whole complete

explanation.walkthrough: The question-and-answer shape suggests a conversation, but each half is a meaning; the mathematical sense is 'of or being an integer'.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the word concerns integers, and in everyday use it means fundamental and necessary to the whole.

clue.text: Snare's component inverted

indicators.note: something inverted is turned upside down, which in a down entry flips the order

blocks.note: a component is a part

explanation.surface: A piece of a snare drum turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snare' suggests the drum, with a component flipped over, but it means a device for catching animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a noose or device for catching animals, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Generals call this a warm place to relax

blocks.note: first meaning: the order to start shooting
second meaning: a fireplace with a burning hearth

explanation.walkthrough: The military command to start shooting and a cosy grate in a living room share the same two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Commanders order troops to begin shooting with this phrase, and it also names an uncovered domestic hearth burning logs.

clue.text: Artist arrived earlier with something to capture images

indicators.note: earlier means coming before, so one piece is placed in front of the other

blocks.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter turned up early, bringing a device for taking pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The device records photographs or film, so it is a tool for taking pictures.

clue.text: Maniacal despots impounding 1,000 computers

indicators.note: maniacal means wildly crazed, so the letters are thrown into disorder
to impound is to seize and hold, so one piece is kept inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Mad tyrants confiscating a thousand computers.
explanation.walkthrough: K for a thousand comes from kilo, as in kilogram; it sits inside the rearranged tyrants.
explanation.definitionFit: These are personal computers designed to sit on a table, so they are a kind of computer.

clue.text: Headcases racing with oars, loudly

indicators.note: loudly means out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to scull is to row with oars

explanation.surface: Crazy people in a noisy rowing race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headcases' looks like slang for lunatics, but read literally it is the bony case around the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony structure enclosing the brain is literally a case for the head, a playful split of the slang word.
